q: Material is received in a depot against a purchase order and a Receipt Note is posted, but the supplier bill has not yet been paid. How is Purchase Suspense (P.7120) affected?

options.A: It is debited, because every receipt is debited to Purchase Suspense
options.B: It is credited, because material received is credited to Purchase Suspense before bill payment
options.C: It is not affected until the bill is paid
options.D: It is credited to Sales Suspense instead

q: A supplier is given an advance payment before any material is received. What is the effect on Purchase Suspense (P.7120)?

options.A: It is credited, because Purchase Suspense can never be debited first
options.B: It is credited to Sales Suspense
options.C: It has no effect on any suspense head
options.D: It is debited, as an advance payment is the exception that puts a debit first in Purchase Suspense

q: A purchaser deposits auction money, including EMD held for the sale, but the material has not yet been delivered. Where is the money watched?

options.A: In Sales Suspense (P.7140) as a credit, because money is received first and delivery follows later
options.B: Directly as a reduction of Stores in Stock
options.C: In Purchase Suspense (P.7120) as a debit
options.D: In Stock Adjustment Account as a debit

q: Stock verification shows the priced ledger exceeds the ground stock for an item. How is the shortage brought to account?

options.A: Sales Suspense is debited and Stock is credited
options.B: Stock Adjustment Account is debited and Stores in Stock is credited
options.C: Stores in Stock is debited and Stock Adjustment Account is credited
options.D: The shortage is quietly added to issues with no separate entry

q: Stock verification finds ground stock in excess of the priced ledger for an item. What is the correct booking?

options.A: Stores in Stock is debited and Stock Adjustment Account is credited
options.B: Stock Adjustment Account is debited and Stores in Stock is credited
options.C: Sales Suspense is credited and Stock is debited
options.D: No entry is needed for an excess

q: Material is issued from a depot to a consuming work against an Issue Note. How does Stores in Stock under PH 71 move?

options.A: It is debited, because issues increase stock
options.B: It is credited, because issued material leaves stock and its cost is charged to the consuming work or final head
options.C: It remains unchanged until the work is completed
options.D: It is debited at the original purchase price of the lot

q: After material was received and Purchase Suspense was credited, the supplier bill is passed for payment. How is Purchase Suspense cleared to that extent?

options.B: It is credited again when the bill is passed
options.C: It is debited when the bill is passed for payment
options.D: It is transferred to Sales Suspense

q: Material sold earlier, against money already held in Sales Suspense, is now delivered through a Sale Issue Note. What happens?

options.A: Sales Suspense is credited again and Stock is debited
options.B: Purchase Suspense is credited and Stock is debited
options.C: No entry is needed because money was received earlier
options.D: Sales Suspense is debited by contra and Stores in Stock is credited on delivery

q: At the end of a quarter, a balance remains uncleared in the Stock Adjustment Account. With whose sanction is it cleared?

options.A: With the sanction of the depot storekeeper alone
options.B: It is cleared automatically without any sanction
options.C: With the sanction of the purchaser
options.D: With the sanction of the GM / AGM

q: Depot X transfers stock to Depot Y. How do the two depots record the movement in Stores Suspense?

options.A: Both depots debit Stores in Stock
options.B: Both depots credit Stores in Stock
options.C: Depot X credits Stores in Stock as transfers-out and Depot Y debits Stores in Stock as transfers-in
options.D: Depot X debits and Depot Y credits Stores in Stock
